reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) does not support the key premises. E1 discusses oxidation of a Cr-Ta-Al RHEA forming CrTaO4, not alumina barrier coatings on NbMoTaW. E2 shows that Al content in a CoCrNiAl alloy leads to Al2O3 formation, but it does not involve ALD coatings, graded adhesion layers, or the NbMoTaW system. The premises about ALD coating efficacy, graded layer mitigation of mismatch, and specific performance on NbMoTaW are entirely unsupported by the provided passages.
premises: Alumina coatings can act as effective oxygen diffusion barriers at high temperatures.
Atomic layer deposition (ALD) can produce thin, conformal, dense alumina coatings.
A graded adhesion layer can mitigate thermal expansion mismatch and prevent spallation.
NbMoTaW alloy lacks inherent oxidation resistance and forms non-protective scales at 1200°C.
A 50 nm ALD alumina coating can remain intact and protective for 10 hours at 1200°C in pure oxygen.
